scope: Independent static review of four private real-child setup/cache tests, exact baseline/after unified patch, and their owning cleanup observations. Findings reported separately from SDK design review.

findings.problem: workers_settled only observes is_finished, which is also true for a panicked worker. Consuming its handle occurs even when join returns Err. The first partial-ACK/stdout-closed failure is retained by get_or_insert, masking the later join failure, so the tests can pass and print created_workers_finished=true despite a worker panic.
findings.required_revision: Observe actual per-created-worker join outcomes separately from the first cleanup error, using absent/not-joined versus successful/failed states. Assert successful joins for every created worker in these proof cases; retain no invented result for uncreated workers.

findings.problem: Actual Node status can be observed after forced kill or cleanup deadline expiry. node_reaped=true plus the unchanged first failure does not show that these expected EOF cleanup cases avoided forced/deadline cleanup, because their initial failure masks those later states.
findings.required_revision: Emit separately observed force/deadline facts after the actual cached cleanup attempt and assert the intended unforced, in-budget outcome in the proof cases. Preserve browser custody UNKNOWN and do not convert first-error masking into positive cleanup acceptance.

findings.problem: catch_unwind(...).is_err() accepts any Drop panic. It does not prove that ordinary Drop retained the cached fixed cleanup error as its panic payload.
findings.required_revision: Decode the actual panic payload and require the exact expected fixed resident stdout-closed failure, while retaining the observation/channel check that no second cleanup attempt occurred.

accepted_elements: Fault injection is private and occurs after an actual Node child is owned, immediately before the relevant fallible worker creation. Normal new() passes no fault/probe.
Writer/reader/stderr faults preserve the original fixed typed constructor error and exercise real pipe/channel/Drop cleanup; they do not claim actual OS thread exhaustion.
No provider, SDK, credential, browser response, or ACK is fabricated.
Observation is sent through an unbounded private channel only after real cleanup and Result caching; cached returns do not emit another attempt.
The source uses actual child status and real worker handles, and fixed printed metadata explicitly leaves browser custody UNKNOWN.
Repeated close retains the same failed Result; actual receiver disposal supplies the cache test failure trigger.
limits: Source-only change request; no compilation, tests, browser/probe execution, or empirical OS exhaustion proof.
Node reaping and worker completion do not establish Chromium/group absence or temporary-file destruction.
Future Node diagnostic schema/source changes require exact candidate rebase and fresh source bindings before runtime proof.
